topics.title: The substation fire -- what ACTUALLY happened
topics.author: Ray Dunleavy

posts.author: Ray Dunleavy
posts.body:
It has been eight months and we still have not had a straight answer about the Elm Street substation. The Ledger ran four paragraphs in July and then nothing. The county said there would be a report.

What I know for certain:

[list][*]It went up around 4:15 in the afternoon on July 9th.[*]Three quarters of Gridfall was out until the following night, east side until Friday.[*]There was a contractor on site that week doing something to the fencing and the yard lighting.[/list]

What I do not know is why a transformer that was inspected in April caught fire in July. If anyone has the actual incident report I would like to read it.

"Measure twice."

posts.author: Junie Pell
posts.body:
a few people asked for this at the school thing so here it is. its my mothers, shes been making it since the 60s.

[b]HOT MILK CAKE[/b]

4 eggs
2 c sugar
2 c flour
2 tsp baking powder
1 c milk
1 stick butter
1 tsp vanilla

beat the eggs till theyre light, add sugar. sift the flour and baking powder in. heat the milk and butter together till the butter melts (dont boil it) and pour that in with the vanilla. 350 for about 30 min in a 9x13.

its very plain which is the point. we eat it with whatever fruit is going.

posts.author: Nedra Oyelaran
posts.body: This is lovely and I am going to make it Thursday. Thank you Junie.

posts.author: H. Prewitt
posts.body:
A few notes, meant helpfully.

[b]1.[/b] "1 stick butter" is not a measurement. It is a measurement in this country by convention but a stick is 1/2 cup and you should write 1/2 cup.

[b]2.[/b] You do not say salt. Every hot milk cake I have seen from that era has 1/4 to 1/2 tsp salt in it and if her butter was salted that explains it, but then you should say salted butter.

[b]3.[/b] "beat the eggs till theyre light" is doing an enormous amount of work in this recipe. That is five to seven minutes on a stand mixer and the whole cake fails if you stop at two. This is the actual technique and it is the one line you have left vague.

[b]4.[/b] A 9x13 at 350 for 30 minutes will be dry. 25 and check it.

Not criticising your mother. Criticising the transcription.

topics.title: the Signal on 62 -- I taped it again 3/14
topics.author: Curtis Flenn

posts.author: Curtis Flenn
posts.body:
Third time now. Same stretch, between the county line sign and the turn for the quarry, about 1.4 miles. 4.115 MHz upper sideband on the Sony. Started 10:47 pm, ran 6 minutes 20 seconds, stopped mid-group.

Woman's voice, recorded not live, groups of five. Tonight I got:

[code]  41 907  22 118  41 907
  63 004  88 812  63 004
  ...
  (repeats, then cuts)[/code]

The repeat pattern is new. The two previous times it did not repeat. I want to be careful here because I know how this sounds, but the repeats are exact, I went over the tape four times.

I have put the audio up: [url=synth://clipvault.tv/watch/signal-62-0314]signal 62 -- 3/14 tape[/url]. If someone with a better ear than mine wants to write out the groups I would be grateful. The [url=synth://wiki.gridfall.net/wiki/signal-on-62]wiki page[/url] has the logs from the previous two.
posts.signature:
C. Flenn -- Gridfall
log everything. date it. keep the tape.

posts.author: Curtis Flenn
posts.body:
[quote=gnash_88]its a numbers station curtis theres like a hundred of them[/quote]

I know what a numbers station is. I have a shelf of them on cassette.

What I am telling you is that this one is only audible on 1.4 miles of a county road and it is not audible from my house four miles away on the same radio at the same hour, and I have tried that eleven times now. That is not how shortwave propagation works. Either there is something local putting it out or there is something on that stretch of road that is doing something to my receiver, and both of those are interesting and neither of them is Cuba.
